receiptReachRuling.question: Does the corrected acceptanceReceipt block describe the run it names, no more and no less?
receiptReachRuling.onItsOwnFace: YES. Measured field by field, censusV1Representation.acceptanceReceipt now reports a gate that rendered canonical.pdf as covering canonical.pdf: documentsCovered ['canonical.pdf'], documentsNotCovered ['boundary.pdf'], coverage.rastered ['canonical.pdf'], coverage.notRenderedByThisGate ['boundary.pdf'], expectedPages 11 against 11 recomputed pages, and boundaryDigestBindingMeans stating that the boundary hash stops the receipt being read against different bytes and 'is not a statement that the gate rendered it.' The bare coversTheWholeFamily claim is gone from the block. The precise thing VF12 failed — a reader taking boundary.pdf as raster-accepted — is fixed on this block's face.

wordForWordAgainstTheQueueRow.claimMade: coverage.wordsTakenFrom: 'data/rcap-grade-a/packet-factory-24h/RASTER_QUEUE.json, this family's row, coverage block — copied rather than restated so the two records cannot drift'
wordForWordAgainstTheQueueRow.measured: Compared key by key against historicalRasterRows[31].coverage. IDENTICAL, byte for byte: basis, whatCompleteMeansHere, rastered, notRenderedByThisGate. Both prose sentences are the row's own words unaltered. NOT verbatim: the row's 'complete: true' appears in the receipt as 'everyCanonicalDocumentRendered: true', and the row's 'documents' and 'notRastered: []' are not carried.
wordForWordAgainstTheQueueRow.rulingOnTheCopy: The copy is faithful and the two renames are improvements, not drift. 'everyCanonicalDocumentRendered' is exactly what the row's own whatCompleteMeansHere says 'complete' means, and it removes the ambiguity that produced this whole finding. Dropping 'notRastered: []' is correct rather than lossy, because that field is false in the row itself — boundary.pdf was not rastered, and the row says so two keys away in notRenderedByThisGate. This is not the failure.
wordForWordAgainstTheQueueRow.doesTheRowSayWhatIsAttributedToIt: Its coverage block does, verbatim. Its rasterReceipt block, describing the SAME run, says the opposite. See theFailure.

receiptReachRuling.theFailure: The correction was applied to one of the two records that describe run 34058277654, and the corrected record asserts that the two are the same. RASTER_QUEUE.json historicalRasterRows[31].rasterReceipt — same workflow, same run 34058277654, same job 101554484258, same rendered commit 2495d6d9b595a53c4e3cdf3cbeebea94b891d151, same two bound digests — still carries coversTheWholeFamily true, documentsNotCovered [] and whatThisGateDidNotRender []: the three fields the correction removed or inverted. Four keys after the corrected block, censusV1Representation.whyThisReceiptIsTheOne states 'RASTER_QUEUE.json carries exactly this receipt for this family, bound by hash to the two fixtures above.' At this base that sentence is false, and it was made false by this correction. A reader who follows either in-family pointer — wordsTakenFrom or whyThisReceiptIsTheOne — is sent to the queue row and meets the pre-correction overclaim there, with the family record vouching that it is the same receipt. The rationale the new block gives for copying, 'so the two records cannot drift', is defeated in the one field it exists to fix, at the moment it was written.
receiptReachRuling.whyThisIsNotVF12sFindingRestated: VF12 failed the acceptanceReceipt block for what it said. That block now says the right thing. This lane fails a different record — an in-family sentence asserting an identity between two records that materially differ — which VF12 recorded only as supporting because at VF12's base the two records did in fact agree. The correction is what made them disagree, and nothing in the correction says so: correctedOn.whatDidNotChange lists the run, job, rendered commit, digests, page count and whatItDoesNotEstablish, and does not mention that the queue's copy of this receipt was left as it was.
receiptReachRuling.verdict: The receipt describes the run. The family record does not describe the receipt's relationship to the record it cites, and one sentence in it is now false.

WHAT IS NOW RIGHT, EACH RECOMPUTED RATHER THAN READ. canonical.pdf 732e7f47cff8659b30712c3fc0e886c9ac141052955d1aefbb7f3008aa63f845 / 33154 B / 11 pages and boundary.pdf 87e4bf90460e42f74dc220b31c23e90ce16206c43a2ee5d6cc78fd71ac583d58 / 33493 B / 11 pages, with pdfinfo, pdf-lib and the decompressed page-tree /Count all agreeing on 11 and 11. censusV1Representation.fixtures pins exactly those six values. reports/rendered-artifacts.json pins exactly those six values in artifacts[] and pdfs[], its pageManifest assigns all 11 pages correctly, and its everyPageRastered false / rasterSkipped true / rasterPages [] / independentVerificationPending true are honest about the build-time gate and consistent with the corrected block rather than in tension with it. source-receipt.json names no artifact bytes at all. approval-request.json contains no raster claim, no coversTheWholeFamily, and no reference to either fixture; its one settled counsel question carries an express scope limit and its four other questions remain raised. The superseded 10-page and 8-page digests appear nowhere in the family except inside the labelled supersededFixtures block. The corrected acceptanceReceipt block itself is accurate: see receiptReachRuling.onItsOwnFace. Searched across the whole family, 'coversTheWholeFamily' now occurs exactly once, at product-wiring.json line 332, inside correctedOn.was. WHAT IS STILL WRONG. censusV1Representation.whyThisReceiptIsTheOne states 'RASTER_QUEUE.json carries exactly this receipt for this family, bound by hash to the two fixtures above.' Measured against the queue at this base, that is false. historicalRasterRows[31].rasterReceipt describes the identical run — workflow, run 34058277654, job 101554484258, jobConclusion success, rendered commit 2495d6d9b595a53c4e3cdf3cbeebea94b891d151, both bound digests, all nine identifiers equal — and still carries coversTheWholeFamily true, documentsNotCovered [] and whatThisGateDidNotRender [], the three fields 8bb1b82f0 removed or inverted on the family side. The corrected block's own coverage.wordsTakenFrom sends the reader to that same row on the stated ground that copying means 'the two records cannot drift'; the two records drifted at the moment of the copy, in the exact field the copy existed to fix. This is not a bookkeeping nicety: scripts/generate-rcap-grade-a-fulfillment-authority.mjs line 1406 reads raster.rasterReceipt.coversTheWholeFamily === true as the evidence that the raster covered the whole family, and scripts/rcap-route-productization/generate-proven-family-productization-census.mjs line 290 raises problem P21 when it is anything else. For ms-nonconv-set that field is still true. The exposure is latent rather than active — the family sits at notEligible[92], approval-request.json status PENDING_INDEPENDENT_VERIFICATION, approvedForLive false, live false, commercialRoutesOpened 0 — but the record those gates read is the claim VF12 proved false, and it is the record the corrected family block points at. Two supporting points, neither independently disqualifying. First, the same overclaim shape was tested here rather than taken on the commit message's word: across all 255 product-wiring.json files under data/rcap-all50/overlays/census-v1, zero acceptanceReceipt blocks carry it, so 8bb1b82f0's claim that this was the one block is TRUE of family records; across RASTER_QUEUE.json it holds in 167 of 249 rows, so the shape is a factory-wide queue condition and this family's own row is one of them. Second, censusV1Representation.independentVerificationOwed still records VF04 as the only prior read ('VF04 read this family at 513f43c82 ... A re-read of ARTIFACTS against these records is owed before the family can be a complete independent pass'), and does not record VF12's read at f78191545 or its FAIL, even though the correctedOn block four keys earlier is expressly 'on VF12's independent finding'. A reader of that block would count one prior failed read where there are two.
ARTIFACTS.finding: FAIL: the acceptance receipt now states the raster's reach correctly, and the family record still misstates the receipt's relationship to the record it cites. whyThisReceiptIsTheOne says the queue carries exactly this receipt; the queue carries the pre-correction receipt for the same run, with coversTheWholeFamily true and documentsNotCovered [], and a commercial-authority generator reads that field as live evidence. Correcting one of two records that describe the same run, while the corrected one asserts they are identical and cannot drift, moves the overclaim rather than removing it. The repair is narrow: bring historicalRasterRows[31].rasterReceipt into line with the family's corrected block, or qualify whyThisReceiptIsTheOne and wordsTakenFrom to say which record was corrected and which was not.

routeLinePlacementRuling.causeEstablishedFromTheBuilder: This lane did not stop at the geometry. scripts/build-census-v1-ms-nonconv-set.mjs line 370 pushes the Route line immediately BEFORE 'SO ORDERED.' in the proposed_order branch, and the comment above it records why: the trailer 'used to be the last ink on the order's second page, below "JUDICIAL OFFICER OF THE COURT", below "(the Court alone completes, signs and enters this order)" and below "APPROVED AS TO FORM, for the prosecuting authority:" -- machine text inside a band the page itself assigns to the Court', and it was deliberately hoisted above the execution band. The same move is made at line 312 for the petition, above the notary's verification sheet, and the comment records FIX35 making it on the Rhode Island host. The global trailer at line 455 is what puts the line at the foot of the other five pages.
routeLinePlacementRuling.disposition: AN OBSERVATION THAT FAILS NONE OF THE FIFTEEN. Reached independently, and it does not adopt VF12's reading of the cause. CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP: measured on page 7 — 0 words outside the page box, 0 outside the 72 pt margin box, 0 overlapping word pairs, and about 19 pt of clear space between the Route block and 'SO ORDERED.' PAGE_ORDER: the pageManifest assigns packetPage 7 to proposed_order sourcePage 2 and that is what page 7 is. PROTECTED_FIELDS: the Court's band is intact, blank and disclaimed, and the Route line sits above it rather than inside it. No other obligation of the fifteen reaches page typography.
routeLinePlacementRuling.whereThisDiffersFromVF12: VF12 recorded that the placement 'reads as a spill from the end of page 6 rather than a footer.' The geometry supports that reading, but the builder shows the cause is the opposite of accidental: the line is not a footer in this component at all, it is a flow element positioned by design before the decretal and execution band, and it lands at the top of page 7 only because the order's body fills page 6. Both lanes rule it no failure; they should not be read as agreeing on why.
routeLinePlacementRuling.thePointThisLaneWouldPassToAnAppearanceL: Not that the line is too high, but that on a continuation page it becomes the first thing a judge reads, under no caption. Moving it lower on page 7 would put machine text back inside the Court's band, which is the defect the builder comment says was already fixed once. If anyone acts on this, the safe change is to suppress the trailer on a continuation sheet, not to relocate it below the signature. This lane makes no such change and treats it as no obligation's failure.
